q1: SELECT b1.name AS bar1, b2.name AS bar2 FROM bar AS b1, bar AS b2 WHERE NOT EXISTS(SELECT s1.beer FROM serves AS s1 WHERE s1.bar = b1.name AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM serves AS s2 WHERE s2.bar = b2.name AND s2.beer = s1.beer)) AND EXISTS(SELECT s2.beer FROM serves AS s2 WHERE s2.bar = b2.name AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM serves AS s1 WHERE s1.bar = b1.name AND s1.beer = s2.beer))
q2: SELECT barsbeer1.name, barsbeer2.name FROM (SELECT barsbeer.name AS name, COUNT(barsbeer.name) AS count FROM (SELECT b1.name FROM bar AS b1 LEFT JOIN serves ON b1.name = serves.bar) AS barsbeer GROUP BY barsbeer.name) AS barsbeer1, (SELECT barsbeer.name AS name, COUNT(barsbeer.name) AS count FROM (SELECT b1.name FROM bar AS b1 LEFT JOIN serves ON b1.name = serves.bar) AS barsbeer GROUP BY barsbeer.name) AS barsbeer2 WHERE barsbeer1.count < barsbeer2.count

explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not equivalent. Q1 checks for bars that serve all beers served by another bar and at least one beer that no other bar serves. Q2, on the other hand, is trying to find bars that serve a different number of beers than another bar, which is not the same as the conditions in Q1.
counterexample_dsp: Create two bars, BarA and BarB, where BarA serves beer X and beer Y, and BarB serves beer X. BarA should be the result of Q1 but not of Q2.
